A partnership framework requires measurable monitoring and effective issue resolution to translate outreach into sustained participation; the source records these mechanisms but not their outcomes.
argumentsFor: Targeted outreach, onboarding assistance, capacity building and handholding can reduce entry barriers for tribal enterprises.
TICCI’s mobilisation and field-level support can connect entrepreneurs with GeM opportunities, while GeM provides training resources, onboarding facilitation and issue-resolution mechanisms.
Joint action plans, progress monitoring and entrepreneur feedback can support iterative improvement.
background: GeM is described in the source as the national public procurement portal. The MoU with TICCI is designed to strengthen participation of tribal entrepreneurs and enterprises in government procurement.

mainsPractice.stem: Evaluate how the GeM–TICCI partnership can promote inclusive public procurement for tribal entrepreneurs. Discuss the institutional mechanism and implementation conditions required for durable participation.

officialFacts.text: GeM signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Tribal Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (TICCI) on 20 November 2026.
The collaboration aims to connect tribal businesses with public procurement opportunities through targeted outreach, capacity building, onboarding assistance and sustained handholding support.

example.heading: Illustration
example.text: Illustration: If a tribal enterprise is unfamiliar with GeM registration, TICCI’s field support and mentoring could help it understand onboarding, while GeM’s training and issue-resolution support could assist its participation. This is a hypothetical application, not a reported event.

pocketRead.excerpt: The GeM–TICCI MoU combines tribal-enterprise mobilisation by TICCI with GeM’s onboarding, training and issue-resolution support to widen procurement access.

question.answer: The partnership can improve inclusion by combining TICCI’s local mobilisation and field support with GeM’s training, onboarding and issue-resolution mechanisms. Its success would depend on sustained handholding, joint monitoring and feedback-based correction; the source does not report outcomes yet.
question.prompt: How can the GeM–TICCI partnership convert a digital procurement platform into more inclusive access for tribal entrepreneurs?

sections.heading: A partnership built around access
paragraphs: On 20 November 2026, GeM signed an MoU with TICCI to strengthen tribal entrepreneurs’ participation in government procurement. The mechanism pairs TICCI’s identification, mobilisation, outreach and field support with GeM’s training, onboarding and issue-resolution assistance.

sections.heading: From onboarding to sustained participation
paragraphs: The arrangement is intended to address the gap between a platform’s formal availability and an enterprise’s practical ability to use it. Joint action plans, progress monitoring and entrepreneur feedback are intended to improve participation, but the source does not establish results or quantify beneficiaries.
